A quick brush-on treatment stopped tooth decay in a major US trial.

Silver diamine fluoride is dabbed onto decayed teeth, where silver targets bacteria and fluoride strengthens remaining tooth. In a trial across Michigan, New York and Iowa, researchers treated 830 children under 6 with severe decay. Applied every six months, it halted decay in more than half of affected teeth.

The treatment could spare young children drilling and fillings, sometimes requiring sedation or general anesthesia. Lead researcher Margherita Fontana says it is effective and safe, even for children as young as 1.

The trade-off: treated areas turn permanently black. The FDA has approved it for tooth sensitivity; researchers say the findings support approval for cavity treatment.

[Fontana M, Moursi A, Gonzalez-Cabezas C, et al. JAMA Pediatrics. 2026. DOI: 10.1001/jamapediatrics.2026.2567]
